audit.whatIsWrong: Five of the seven chart rows contradicted the packet chart and this page's own prose. The chart gave Irelia Level 1 while whys[0] says he out-pokes you; it gave Kennen Level 3 while whys[2] says your E flips the lane; it gave Kennen First item while whys[5] says you win the skirmish there; it gave Irelia Level 6 while whys[4] says his R chain-stuns you out of the combo.
audit.why: Both layers agreed with each other and both were wrong the same way, so no existing check caught it. The packet chart matches every why on the page.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with matching ratings. Rows 1 (Skill) and 6 (Kennen) were already right.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] sits in the Levels 4-5 row but describes the first-item spike, duplicating whys[5]. The Level 3 window is never given Flawless Duet's cooldown, so 'trade around your E' has no number attached.
audit.why: An off-by-one why means the reader gets no advice at all for levels 4-5, the exact stretch where Kennen's Q drops to a 5.5s cooldown and his poke starts adding up.
audit.corrected: whys[3] rewritten for the real Levels 4-5 stage with Flawless Duet's rank-3 13s cooldown; Slicing Maelstrom's flat 120s added to spikes[3] as the punish window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings tell the player to use Defiant Dance (W) to block, eat or channel through Thundering Shuriken and Electrical Surge. Riot's text for Defiant Dance says she takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge. Kennen's entire kit is magic damage, so the page's central defensive instruction does nothing.
audit.why: This is the same class of error as telling a Kassadin to shield Irelia's physical damage with a magic shield — the player holds a button expecting mitigation that never arrives, and eats the third Mark of the Storm while doing it.
audit.corrected: Every 'W blocks his poke' claim replaced. The real defensive rule is mark-counting: Mark of the Storm stuns on the third application, so you step out at two rather than tanking a fourth source of magic damage. Kennen's zero-mana energy bar is also stated as why cooldown-tracking, not mana-tracking, is the read.

edits.before: Your W (Defiant Dance) channel now blocks his shuriken and zap, but you still lack a stun to punish him — it's even.
edits.after: Defiant Dance (W) cuts physical only, so it barely dents his magic poke — you deny the wave, he can't kill you. Even.

edits.before: Your first-item spike gives full reset uptime plus on-hit and armor/MR shred — you're a lane tyrant who sticks through his move speed.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours: Flawless Duet is back every 13 seconds at rank 3, and each Mark it leaves turns into a Bladesurge reset he can't outrun.

edits.before: His R (Slicing Maelstrom) is the danger window — it stacks Marks of the Storm fast enough to chain-stun, and with a gank he locks you out of your dash combo and bursts you down.
edits.after: His R (Slicing Maelstrom) is the danger window — it stacks Marks of the Storm fast enough to chain-stun you out of your dash combo. It is 120 seconds flat: spend it, and two waves are yours.

edits.before: W (Defiant Dance) the moment he commits his shuriken or zaps a mark, eating the burst, then E-stun in once your block is up
edits.after: Count his Marks of the Storm, not his health bar — step out at two, because the third is a free stun and Defiant Dance won't blunt it

edits.before: Kennen's Q (shuriken) and his W (Electrical Surge) auto-marks are the whole early game — he chips you from range while you have only Q and no stun, so don't walk into shuriken range to throw a dash he can just back off from. Farm with Q-resets off the wave and save W (Defiant Dance) to eat the shuriken or the W zap when he commits. At level 3, E (Flawless Duet) flips it: now you E-stun in, the E MARKS him so Bladesurge resets onto him, and you finally make him pay for stepping up — just don't sit in lane long enough to take a third Mark of the Storm.
edits.after: Thundering Shuriken (Q) and Electrical Surge (W) auto-marks are the whole early game — he chips you from 950 range while you have only Q and no stun, so don't walk in to throw a dash he can back off from. Farm Q-resets off the wave, and don't expect Defiant Dance (W) to help: it reduces physical damage and every spell he owns is magic. At level 3, Flawless Duet (E) flips it: E-stun in, the Mark makes him a Bladesurge reset target, and you finally punish a step-up — just never stand there holding two Marks of the Storm.

edits.before: This is your window. With E up and your first item online, you bait the zap, W (Defiant Dance)-channel through his shuriken to block the burst, then E-stun in and chain Bladesurge resets off the wave and his minions so his move speed can't kite you off. The catch is level 6 — his R (Slicing Maelstrom) stacks Marks of the Storm fast enough to stun-chain, so do not all-in when his ult plus a jungler can lock you out of your dash combo. Force the fight when his R is down and you out-trade him cleanly before three marks land.
edits.after: This is your window. With E up and your first item online, step in on the shuriken's cooldown rather than through it — 5.5 seconds at rank 3 — then E-stun and chain Bladesurge resets off the wave and his minions so his move speed can't kite you off. He runs on energy, so cooldowns are the only read you get. The catch is level 6: Slicing Maelstrom stacks Marks fast enough to stun-chain, so never all-in when his ult plus a jungler can lock you out. Fight when his R is down and you win cleanly.

notes: Central error: four strings instructed the player to block Kennen's poke with Defiant Dance, which Riot's own text says reduces physical damage — Kennen deals magic damage across his whole kit. Replaced with mark-counting, which is the real defensive rule. Five chart rows were inverted against both the packet and the page's own whys; flipped as one matched group with ratings. Kennen's Lightning Rush is a form change, not a blink — no claim is made about grounding or walling it, since the kit text does not support one.
